title: DEFINE stage gates D1..D8 as pure check functions
description: rcf-lite gains src/query/gates.js with one check function per stage D1..D8. Each function takes (tree, ledgers, profile, scope) and returns { stage, gate, state, checks[] } where every check is { name, ok, over: 'delta'|'tree', pass, total, failing: [{ id, why }] }. Stage state is 'passed' | 'failing' | 'acknowledged' (only for D3, D5, D6 and only when the freeze record acknowledges that gate at the current hash) | 'notApplicable' (the stage decides that itself from the scope per the proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 3.2 rules and the summary table in section 2.7). Blocking in 0.29.0: D1 brief, D2 skeleton, D4 floors (every REQ in scope has a US; every US in scope has a testable AC, a failure AC and a must-not AC, or a reasoned opt-out per class; tacIds non-empty and resolving; no scaffold placeholder), D7 decisions, D8 freeze (prior gates passed or acknowledged at the current hash, every AC owned by exactly one FBS, queue head actionable and not a placeholder, validate clean; preflight and ui-baseline presence as the section 3.2 rules specify). Warn-with-ack in 0.29.0: D3, D5, D6 build only the cheap data-backed checks (D3: every TAC in scope has at least one interface and each interface kind is in the closed vocabulary of section 5.2; D5: TAD securityArchitecture present when any auth or httpApi REQ exists, operationalConcerns present when deployed-scope ACs exist, concern-ledger entries applied or waived where they exist; D6: validate clean tree-wide plus open probe-ledger count). The D3 template parser, entity join, D5 catalogue, D6 contradiction and unsatisfiable scans, and the probe runner are 0.30 and left as named seams. AC class is a bracketed prefix on AC description ('[failure] ...', '[must-not] ...', '[happy]', '[edge]', '[non-functional]', decision 6); opt-out per class reuses the existing manifest.baselineAcOptOuts[] array with a baselineKey of the shape 'defineD4:failure' or 'defineD4:mustNot' (recorded in ADR-4122). No storage state, no 'stale' state. ADR-4126 (0.29.0) amendment: every gate check declares an owning persona, `productOwner` or `engineer`, and a one-sentence `question` in that persona’s register. A check that would need both personas is split so every check is homogeneous: `skeleton:reqFields` becomes `skeleton:reqIntent` (productOwner: description + domain) + `skeleton:reqShape` (engineer: shapeClassification.shapes); `decisions:allAnswered` becomes `decisions:wellFormed` (productOwner: enumerated per #241 format) + `decisions:allAnswered` (engineer: zero open). A new D3 check `shapes:draftSettled` fails every interface whose description still carries the leading `[draft]` marker so an L1-pre-populated interface stays distinguishable from one the engineer has settled. 0.30.0 PR 5 (ADR-4131) amendment: D3, D5 and D6 run the substantive checks of proposal 3.2 and exit 4 under `--check`; `--ack` remains their recorded override. D4 reports closed sets and `ownerRef` resolution as findings. D2 validates `resolvedBy` pointers and the standards citation. The three D3 bite checks land in this PR: `shapes:templateMarkers` (per-kind marker presence on `interfaces[].description`, over delta, ids `<tacId>:<name>`, why names the missing marker, drafts included), `shapes:entityJoin` (every `coreEntities[].name` named by exactly one `recordShape` tree-wide, ids `TAD.entity:<name>` with 'no record shape' or 'N record shapes'), `shapes:pathsResolve` (any `path:`-like token in an interface description resolves against `resolvedPaths` in the stage context or the description carries `authoredAt: D3`, over delta). The CLI readiness `--check shapes` exits 4 on an unacknowledged D3 failure and 0 when acked at the current hash; `ackable(stage)` returns true for D3, D5, D6 and false for D1, D2, D4, D7, D8; `--ack` on D1, D2, D4, D7 or D8 exits 2 unchanged. DEFINE step 3 rulings R2, R5, R6, R7, R8 2026-10-05 (w-2026-10-05-dave-001): `shapes:draftSettled` is a tree-wide check that runs regardless of the D3 scope's own early-return (R2); `shapes:entityJoin` is tree-wide by definition and runs before any `notApplicable` short-circuit via the shared helper ADR-4138 lands (R5); `extractInterfacePathTokens` honours a short whitelist of known bare repo names so `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, `LICENSE`, `Procfile`, `Containerfile`, `Justfile`, `Rakefile`, `Gemfile` and `CODEOWNERS` are checked by `shapes:pathsResolve` (R6; the slash-or-extension rule stays for everything else, and the whitelist is exported for tests); `skeleton:standardsCited` runs tree-wide regardless of the D2 scope's own early-return and shares the ADR-4138 helper (R7); and for `standards:<pack>` concern-ledger entries both `applied` and `waived` dispositions satisfy `skeleton:standardsCited` alongside a citation (R8; the check question reads 'Every registered standards pack is cited, applied or waived').
rationale: Baz ruled on 2026-09-22 (proposal section 9, decision 2) that gates block where the data exists and warn-with-ack for D3, D5 and D6 until 0.31 (Baz ruled 2026-09-24 that 0.31 renumbers to 0.30, so this train ships D3/D5/D6 as warn-with-ack in 0.29.0). One check function per stage is the seam every later consumer reads: the readiness view (REQ-175) composes them, the freeze verb (slice 3) refuses on any failing stage, the viewer's Readiness tab (slice 5) prints the same checks[]. Building the check functions now, with cheap data-backed checks only, keeps 0.29.0 shippable while leaving named seams for 0.30's template parser, entity join, catalogue walk, probe runner and consistency scans.
